newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi party leader under house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Burundi party leader under house arrest.

text.p: The secretary general of the Frodebu political party which ran Burundi up until a military coup last July has been placed under house arrest, a party official said on Sunday.
A Frodebu spokesman said no reason had been given for Augustin Nzogibwani's house arrest.

Frodebu, mainly backed by the majority Hutu ethnic group, won the country's first multi-party elections in 1993 and led the government until Major Pierre Buyoya -- a Tutsi and Burundi's president from 1987 to 1993 -- took over in a military coup last July.
Burundi's army, controlled by the minority Tutsi who ruled Burundi for centuries before independence in 1962, is fighting against rebel Hutu militia. Tens of thousands have died.
Regional African states have imposed economic sanctions on Burundi and have demanded the restoration of democratic rule.
